text: Silicon is an efficient laser gain medium, so III-V materials are unnecessary for building light sources directly on a silicon photonic chip.
explanation: False: silicon's indirect bandgap makes it a poor light emitter, so it cannot lase efficiently. On-chip sources therefore rely on heterogeneous integration, wafer-bonding III-V gain material (InP, GaAs) to the silicon and coupling evanescently into the waveguide.
